power.power-input-dc: rated -48 to -60 VDC, operating -40 to -72 VDC, 40 A maximum (guide Table 26)

ac-b2f.description: QFX5220-32CD-AFI: two 1600 W AC supplies (JPSU-1600W-1UACAFI) and six back-to-front fan modules (QFX5220-32CD-FANAI). All have a Juniper azure blue handle and the label AIR IN (guide Tables 3, 16 and 18).

ac-f2b.description: QFX5220-32CD-AFO: two 1600 W AC supplies (JPSU-1600W-1UACAFO) and six front-to-back fan modules (QFX5220-32CD-FANAO). All have a Juniper gold handle and the label AIR OUT (guide Tables 3, 16 and 18).

chas.description: QFX5220-32CD-CHAS, the spare chassis, shipped without power supplies or fan modules. They are ordered separately, as AC or DC supplies and AIR OUT or AIR IN fan modules. Supplies and fans of one airflow only go in. The supply and fan bays are shown open.

dc-b2f.description: QFX5220-32CD-D-AFI: two 1600 W DC supplies (JPSU-1600W-1UDCAFI) and six back-to-front fan modules. Each supply has a single feed, so feeds A and B go one to each.

dc-f2b.description: QFX5220-32CD-D-AFO: two 1600 W DC supplies (JPSU-1600W-1UDCAFO) and six front-to-back fan modules. Each supply has a single feed, so feeds A and B go one to each.

description: Juniper QFX5220-32CD, a 1RU 400G data-centre spine and leaf switch that runs Junos OS Evolved. It has 32 QSFP-DD ports (400, 100, 40, 25 or 10 GbE, channelizable) in two rows of sixteen and two SFP+ ports (10 GbE only). All ports are on the port side, and each has a lamp beside it. The port side also carries an RJ-45 time-of-day port and four clock connectors (PPS and 10 MHz, in and out). It has an RJ-45 console port, an RJ-45 management port, a USB port, the reset button, three chassis lamps and the ESD point. The rear carries two power supplies, one at each end, and six fan modules between them. It ships as one front panel in four power and airflow variants, AC or DC supplies with front-to-back (AIR OUT) or back-to-front (AIR IN) airflow. A spare chassis has no supplies and no fan modules.

gaps.wanted: Packet rate, buffer size and latency. The guide states none of them. They are in the QFX5220 datasheet, and Juniper's addresses for it redirect to an hpe.com PSNow page that did not answer when tried, so the datasheet was not read.
The depth of the fan module and of the power supplies. The guide's figures are photographs and isometrics with no scale, and its tables state weights only for the whole chassis.

What the green and amber windows at the corners of the upper (console) RJ-45 jack are. The photograph shows them on both jacks of the stacked shield. The guide describes lamps for the management port only (Table 15) and none for the console. They are not drawn on the console jack.

The speeds of the management jack. Callout 4 of figure 22 says "100 Mbps/1000 Mbps/10000 Mbps". The lamp table (Table 15) describes 10 Mbps, 100 Mbps and 1 Gbps. The jack is modelled at 1g, the highest speed Table 15 describes.
Whether the time-of-day RJ-45 jack has lamps. The photograph shows none, and the guide describes none.

The connector type of the four clock jacks. The guide calls them "clock input and output connectors" and "PTP and external clock connections" and names no type. The photograph shows gold coaxial jacks 6.7 mm across, drawn as the library's SMA jack. Estimated. The QFX5220-128C figure 17 calls its equivalent jacks "SMB", and the 128C text calls them PPS and 10 MHz connectors, so the type may be SMB.
The USB revision. The guide says "USB 2.0/3.0 standard" for the one port. The port is drawn with the kit's neutral usb2 skin.
The vertical rating label at the right end of the rear. It is not legible in the guide's photograph and is not drawn.

The AC and DC power draw. The guide's Tables 19 and 26 say typical 310 W and maximum 834 W (AC) and 328 W and 860 W (DC). Juniper's Hardware Compatibility Tool says 378 W average and 730 W maximum (AC) and 383 W and 877 W (DC). The guide's figures are carried.

The rack ears' positions and the rack kits' contracts. The guide names QFX5K-4PST-RMK-E and QFX5220-32CD-4PRMK and gives two different rail spacings. No kit contract exists in the library and none is written here.

esd.description: the wrist-strap ESD point on the port side (guide figure 22, callout 11)

fan-leds.description: The round status lamp beside each fan slot - green when the module is healthy, amber blinking on an error (guide Table 17).

attrs.redundancy-note: QFX5220 hardware guide, QFX5220 Component Redundancy: the QFX5220-32CD has six fan modules and can operate with one not in operation; the failure of more than one can trigger chassis alarms and shutdown

mgmt.mixed: the out-of-band cluster at the right of the port side - an RJ-45 console port, an RJ-45 management port, a USB port and the recessed reset button. Four kinds, one purpose: reaching and recovering the switch when the data plane cannot.

attrs.redundancy-note: two supplies, each able to carry the whole switch; one may be removed at a time while the switch runs

qsfpdd-leds.description: One bicolour lamp per QSFP-DD port, in the column of lamps left of each pair of columns (guide Table 6).

sfp-plus.description: Ports 32 and 33 as printed, rel-pos carrying the printed number, since the origin token cannot express a block that starts at 32.

sfp-plus-leds.description: Two lamps per SFP+ port - link and activity at the left, status at the right (guide Table 7).

status-leds.description: The three chassis lamps ALM, SYS and ID (guide Table 14).

timing.mixed: the time and frequency block at the left of the port side - an RJ-45 time-of-day port and four clock connectors (PPS and 10 MHz, in and out). Five jacks of two kinds, one purpose: moving a timing reference into or out of the switch.

name: qfx5220-32cd

chassis.note: guide Table 32: 1.72 in (4.3 cm) high, 17.26 in (43.8 cm) wide, 21.1 in (53.59 cm) deep, 24.5 lb (11.11 kg) with power supplies and fans installed, 1RU. The inch figures are used and the centimetre ones in the same cell are rounded copies of them. Juniper's Hardware Compatibility Tool gives the same figures (4.3688 x 43.8404 x 53.594 cm). The width is the body: Table 34 says the outer edges of the front brackets extend it to 19 in, so the brackets are not part of the body and are not modelled. The table does not say whether the depth includes the handles of the supplies and fans.

clock-connectors.note: Left of the first pair of columns, under the RJ-45 time-of-day jack: four gold coaxial jacks 6.7 mm across in two columns and two rows. The left column prints PPS and the right column 10M. The upper row prints OUT between the columns and the lower row IN. Guide figure 22 callout 10 says "PTP and external clock connections" and the guide's text says "Clock input and output connectors (10 MHz and 1 PPS)". The columns sit at 17.1 and 28.1 mm and the rows at 29.8 and 37.6 mm (centres).

colour.note: The front plate samples #8a8a8b (the colour the QFX5130-32CD photograph gave) and is kept, because figure 14 is a small JPEG with a warm cast. The photographs are lit warmly and these are their values, not a paint reference.

drawing-vs-photo.note: Figure 14 and figure 22 are the same photograph of the real unit, so the printing in them agrees. The figure 15 rear shows orange fans and supplies with AIR OUT chips, the front-to-back build, which is the default configuration here. The management jacks show lamps on both jacks in the photograph, while the guide's text describes lamps for the management port only. The photograph is followed.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED, provenance only. The guide names the rack mount kits QFX5K-4PST-RMK-E (four-post rails, brackets and spacers, shipped in the box) and QFX5220-32CD-4PRMK (a spare four-post kit with front and rear mounting rails), and says the front and rear rails must be 28 in (71.1 cm) to 36 in (91.4 cm) apart. The guide's site section says 23.6 to 36 in. The two ranges disagree. No kit contract is written here and `chassis.ears` and `chassis.kits` are left out. The modelled body is the 438.4 mm chassis, without brackets.

front-blue-tab.note: A light-blue tab at the lower right, 16.8 mm wide and about 3.4 mm high, is the chassis serial number slide-out tab, callout 8 of figure 22. It is drawn as decor, because it is a label card and not a part the library models.

gate-1.note: The front photograph (figure 14), between its left and right edges, is 1311 px wide and 128 px from the top edge to the bottom edge, an aspect of 10.24 against the table's 438.4 / 43.7 = 10.03 (2.1 percent out: the top lip shows in the photograph). Scale 2.990 px/mm across, used on both axes with the origin at the left edge and the top edge. The rear photograph (figure 15) is 1309 px wide, 2.986 px/mm. Both photographs are small, so every position read from them is good to about 0.3 mm and is estimated.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life announcement. No Juniper notice was found and the guide, published 2026-10-14, states none. The third-party trackers searched list nothing for the QFX5220. The device states none announced. Estimated, because the trackers are not the maker.

logo.note: The maker's logo and its lockup are printed at the lower right of the face, above the model name QFX5220-32CD. The logo is not drawn: a logo-zone region is reserved where it stands, and the model name is drawn as plain text.

mgmt-panel.note: Right of the SFP+ pair, from the left: a stacked pair of RJ-45 jacks in one shield 17.1 mm wide, a USB-A port standing on its side, and under it the RESET pinhole. Above the jacks the face prints "CON up-arrow, down-arrow MGMT", so the upper jack is the console and the lower the management port (callouts 5 and 4 of figure 22). Each jack shows a green lamp at one corner and an amber one at the other. The guide describes lamps for the management port only (Table 15), so the console jack's lamps are not drawn and are a gap. The USB mark is printed above the port. At the left of the face are the three chassis lamps ALM, SYS and ID with their legends (callout 2) and the round ESD point with its warning mark (callout 11). The lamps stand in a column at 31.8 mm, 5.0, 8.0 and 11.0 mm down. The ESD socket is at 8.7 mm and 33.4 mm down and is 3.8 mm across.

modules.note: The six fan modules (QFX5220-32CD-FANAO and -FANAI, Table 16) and the two power supplies (JPSU-1600W-1UACAFO and -AFI, JPSU-1600W-1UDCAFO and -AFI, Tables 3, 18 and 25) are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay. Each supply carries its own small fan inside (the cooling system is six fan modules and a single fan in each supply). The status lamp of each fan is on the chassis strip beside its slot (figure 31). All four supply components and both fan components already exist in the library under the QFX5130 family names, because the part numbers are the same, and are reused as they are.

port-lamps.note: Table 6 gives each QSFP-DD port one bicolour lamp. Table 7 gives each SFP+ port two lamps (link and activity at the left, status at the right). Figure 14 shows two small round lamp windows, 2.8 mm apart, at the left of every pair of columns in each row, centred 3.4 mm left of the first cage of the pair. The upper window of a row serves the left column's cage and the lower window serves the right column's cage. That assignment is carried over from the QFX5130-32CD, whose guide draws a leader from each window, because this guide draws none, so it is estimated. The lamp heights read 17.4, 20.2, 27.9 and 30.9 mm down. The heights written are 17.0, 19.9, 28.45 and 31.35 mm, the QFX5130-32CD's, which agree to 0.45 mm (about one pixel here) and centre the first and last lamp on their cages. The SFP+ lamps are two round windows above the upper cage, 5.9 mm apart, and two below the lower one. The lamps are unlit in the photograph.

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal in the band between the two rows, read off figure 14 and checked on figure 22: each column prints "n up-arrow, down-arrow n+1", the even number for the upper cage and the odd one for the lower, so the ports run 0 to 31 down each column and left to right. The SFP+ pair prints "32 up-arrow, down-arrow 33". The guide numbers the network ports 0 to 31 and the SFP+ ports 32 and 33 (Table 5 and the Network Ports text). Interface names are not printed. The guide's configuration examples name them et-0/0/N on one FPC and one PIC, both 0, and the show chassis led output lists et-0/0/0 to et-0/0/33. Port N is therefore et-0/0/N, kept here and not in an interfaces block, because the face does not print it.

ports.note: Figure 14: 32 QSFP-DD openings in two rows of 16, each about 56 px (18.7 mm) wide on a 57 px (19.0 mm) pitch, 19.0 mm being the registry's pitch, which is used. They stand in eight pairs of columns, every pair 132 px, 44.15 mm, after the last, so the gutter between pairs is 6.15 mm. The first opening starts at 38.1 mm, so the 19.0 mm cell starts at 37.8. Counts and groups are callout 3 of figure 22 and figure 14. Two SFP+ cages stand to the right of the last pair, an upper one at 388.6 mm and a lower one under it, callout 9. They are single cages, not a ganged block. The upper SFP+ opening measures 11.4 to 21.9 mm down and the lower 26.1 to 35.5, read at 2.99 px/mm.

power.note: Table 19 (AC): 100 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz, 12.7 A at 100 to 127 VAC and 9.4 A at 200 to 240 VAC, typical 310 W and maximum 834 W at 220 to 240 V. Table 26 (DC): rated -48 to -60 VDC, range -40 to -72 VDC, 40 A maximum, typical 328 W and maximum 860 W. The guide's note: maximum measured at 40 C ambient with SR optics at 100 percent load with IMIX traffic; typical at 25 C with DACs at 50 percent load with IMIX traffic, excluding transceivers. Juniper's Hardware Compatibility Tool prints 378 W average and 730 W maximum for AC and 383 W and 877 W for DC. Those differ from the guide in both measures, and the guide's tables are used. The AC pair is the device's, since AC is the default build, and the DC pair is carried under its own keys.

rear-layout.note: Figure 15 at 2.986 px/mm, checked against figure 33: supply slot 0 at the left end, six fan slots numbered 0 to 5 on a 48.96 mm pitch, then supply slot 1 at the right end, and a grey strip before each supply and fan with its power or fan symbol and number. A small round lamp window stands under the fan number. The supply bay measures 54.4 mm by 41 mm from 11.9 mm, the first fan 40.3 mm wide from 76.4 mm on a 146 px pitch, and the right supply starts at 371.4 mm. These agree with the QFX5130-32CD rear to the width of one pixel, and the QFX5130-32CD positions, measured at 4.24 px/mm, are used. The orange fan faces and the black supplies are the library's existing parts. The right end carries a vertical rating label. Fan 0 is the one nearest the left; Table 16 says the fan modules are numbered 0 to 5 counting from left to right.

row-pitch.note: The two QSFP-DD openings of the first column read 12.0 to 20.4 mm and 26.8 to 35.1 mm down (dark bore only, centres 16.2 and 31.0). The registry gives no belly-to-belly row pitch for a QSFP-DD cage. The row pitch 14.35 mm and the top at 12.0 mm come from the same two rows read on the QFX5130-32CD photograph at 4.36 px/mm, which this figure agrees with to 0.5 mm. That is a relative's reading used because this figure is too small to improve on it, and it is estimated.

sources.note: Juniper QFX5220 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2026-10-14, 321 pages (copyright Hewlett Packard Enterprise), from juniper.net. Used here: the front and FRU panel figures 14 and 15, the port panel and management panel figures 22 and 24, Tables 3 and 5 to 7 (components, speeds and port lamps), Tables 14 and 15 (chassis and management lamps), the cooling tables 16 and 17 and figures 28 to 31, the power sections (Tables 18, 19, 25, 26, 29 and figures 33, 34, 37, 39), Table 32 (physical specifications) and Table 31 (environment). The figures 14 and 15 are photographs of the real unit (1500 x 199 px in the PDF, g100343 and g100344). They are read for counts and positions and are not copied. The QFX5220 datasheet could not be read: the maker's address for it (juniper.net/content/dam/www/assets/datasheets and the older assets/us/en/local/pdf/datasheets/1000653-en.pdf) redirects to an hpe.com PSNow page that did not answer when tried, so no datasheet is registered and the datasheet-only figures (forwarding rate, buffer, latency) are left out. The part numbers of the orderable variants come from Juniper's Hardware Compatibility Tool page for the QFX5220-32CD (apps.juniper.net/hct), the maker's own tool. No studio photograph was found on juniper.net, and no Visio stencil or 3D model was found, so the guide's photographs are the only photographs. The guide and the tool are the maker's and public. The guide is copyrighted and nothing in it is copied.

stack-orientation.note: The light latch tongue shows at the foot of the upper cages and at the top of the lower ones in figure 14, so both lips face the band between the rows. The upper cage is upright and the lower one turned 180, the library's stack convention. The figure is too small to settle the tongue on every cage, so this is read from a few cages and carried to all.

tod-jack.note: Callout 1 of figure 22, "RJ-45 grandmaster time-of-day connection", is the RJ-45 jack at the upper left, printed TOD above it. The shield measures 16.7 mm wide and 13.7 mm high from 8.7 mm and 8.0 mm. The latch slot is at the top, so the jack is the library's housing turned 180 degrees. It shows no lamps.

variants.note: Juniper's Hardware Compatibility Tool lists QFX5220-32CD-AFI and -AFO (AC) and QFX5220-32CD-D-AFI and -D-AFO (DC) with the chassis QFX5220-32CD-CHAS, and guide Table 3 names the spare chassis QFX5220-32CD-CHAS "without fan and power module". All five share this front panel and the rear bays, so each is a configuration of this device. The guide also names the DC variant QFX5220-32CD-D (for example in the Junos release note, 19.3R1). NOT MODELLED: the QFX5220-32CD ORv3-compliant switch with tray assembly (QFX522032CDDAFO-T2, 3.65 x 21.14 x 31.5 in, 41 lb), a different mounting for Open Rack v3 racks.

vents.note: Hexagonal holes in the sheet: a band along the top above the cages (about 1.0 to 10.6 mm down), a band along the bottom (about 37.4 to 42.6 mm), a field at the left edge, a column of slots left of the first pair of columns and a field at the right edge. Drawn as vent decor in those positions. Figure 14 shows flat-topped hexagonal holes about 2.9 mm across the points, 6.1 mm apart along a row, with the next row shifted 3.05 mm and 1.72 mm down. The decor tile is set to that pitch, with the lattice phase read at the top band (a hole centre at 39.9 mm across and 2.3 mm down). The positions and the pitch are read at 2.99 px/mm, so the whole feature is estimated.

bottom.empty: Not drawn by any source held. The guide's figures show no underside, and the photographs are of the front and rear only.

placements.description: Table 14 - red steady: major hardware fault; amber steady: minor system alarm; unlit: no alarm or halted
Table 14 - green steady: Junos OS Evolved is loaded; unlit: powered off or halted
Table 14 - blue blinking: the beacon feature is enabled (request chassis beacon fpc 0 on); unlit: not enabled
Table 15 - the status lamp is green steady at 1 Gbps and amber steady at 100 Mbps, unlit at 10 Mbps or link down; the link activity lamp is green steady with a link and blinking with traffic

left.empty: Not drawn by any source held. The mounting figures show the rails on a side wall in perspective only, with no scale from which a hole could be placed.

right.empty: Not drawn by any source held. No figure shows the right wall flat.

top.empty: Not drawn by any source held. The guide gives no figure of the lid, and the photographs are straight-on of the front and rear only.
